rows.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
rows.claim: He reads tanazzalu with a light z, as a form meaning descent.
rows.anchor: قرأ طلحة بن مصرف تنزل خفيفة، من النزول،

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Anas reports that on the Night of Decree Gabriel descends amid angels, praying and greeting every worshipper who remembers God, standing or seated.
rows.anchor: روى قتادة عن أنس أن رسول الله (عليه السلام) قال: «إذا كان ليلة القدر نزل جبرئيل

rows.speaker: كعب ومقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: The Spirit is a class of angels unseen by other angels, descending from sunset until dawn on this night.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب ومقاتل بن حيان: الروح طائفة من الملائكة لا تراهم الملائكة إلا تلك الليلة،

rows.speaker: الواقدي
rows.claim: The Spirit is a great angel, among the greatest in creation, created from the angels.
rows.anchor: وقال الواقدي: هو ملك عظيم [من أعظم الملائكة خلقا] يخلق من الملائكة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels descend by their Lord's permission with every decree God determined for that year until the next, as in God's command in 13:11.
rows.anchor: من كل أمر قدره الله سبحانه وقضاه في تلك السنة إلى قابل، لقوله سبحانه في الرعد: يحفظونه من أمر الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعلي بن أبي طالب وعكرمة
rows.claim: They are reported to read min kulli imri'in salām, instead of min kulli amrin salām.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرأ من كل امرئ سلام، ورويت هذه القراءة أيضا عن علي بن أبي طالب وعكرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation makes the phrase a greeting from every angel.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: إنه وجه معناه إلى الملك أي من كل ملك سلام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another takes min to mean ʿalā: angels send peace upon every Muslim; the source compares this usage with an example of victory over a people.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أن يكون من بمعنى على تقديره: على كل امرئ من المسلمين سلام من الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers the widespread reading because the reading authorities agree on it and it fits the consonantal codices, which have no yāʾ.
rows.anchor: الصحيحة ما عليه العامة لإجماع الحجة من القراءة عليها ولموافقتها خط المصاحف لأنه ليس فيها ياء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He takes salāmun hiya as the end of the preceding sentence at min kulli amr, then a new sentence begins.
rows.anchor: وقوله: سلام هي تمام الكلام عند قوله: من كل أمر ثم ابتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Night of Decree is entirely peace and good, with no evil in it.
rows.anchor: سلام هي أي ليلة القدر سلام وخير كلها ليس فيها شر.

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: God decrees only well-being on this night, whereas on other nights He decrees both affliction and well-being.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك: لا يقدر الله سبحانه في تلك الليلة إلا السلامة،

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The night is safe from Satan, who cannot commit evil or cause harm during it.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: هي سالمة لا يستطيع الشيطان أن يعمل فيها سوءا ولا أن يحدث فيها أذى.

rows.speaker: الشعبي ومنصور بن زاذان
rows.claim: Angels greet the people praying in mosques from sunset to dawn, passing each believer with the greeting Peace be upon you, believer.
rows.anchor: وقال الشعبي ومنصور بن زاذان: هو تسليم الملائكة ليلة القدر على أهل المساجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥattā marks an endpoint and means until the appearance of dawn.
rows.anchor: حتى مطلع الفجر حتى حرف غاية، مجازها إلى مطلع الفجر.

rows.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب والأعمش والكسائي وخلف
rows.claim: They read the lām in maṭliʿ with kasra, meaning the place of rising; the author rejects that noun sense here.
rows.anchor: قرأ يحيى بن وثاب والأعمش والكسائي وخلف بكسر اللام،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers fatḥa in maṭlaʿ: it means the act or time of rising, appropriate to the intended verbal meaning, unlike the place noun with kasra.
rows.anchor: غيرهم بفتحه وهو الاختيار لأن المطلع بفتح اللام بمعنى الطلوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book here are Jews and Christians, and the polytheists are idol worshippers; they had not ceased their disbelief and associationism until the clear proof came.
rows.anchor: وهم اليهود والنصارى، والمشركون وهم عبدة الأوثان، منفكين منتهين عن كفرهم وشركهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Philologists explain munfakkīn as ceasing or disappearing; Arabic usage ma انفكّ فلان يفعل means someone continued doing something, from the root sense of opening or releasing.
rows.anchor: وقال أهل اللغة: زائلين، يقول: العرب: ما انفك فلان يفعل كذا، أي ما زال،

rows.speaker: طرفة
rows.claim: His verse illustrates the Arabic expression for something that does not cease.
rows.anchor: وآليت لا ينفك كشحي بطانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clear proof is Muhammad, who brought the Qur'an, exposed their error and ignorance, and guided them to faith.
rows.anchor: حتى تأتيهم البينة الحجة الواضحة وهي محمد

rows.speaker: ابن كيسان
rows.claim: He interprets the verse as saying they would not abandon their prior description of Muhammad until his mission; after his coming, they split over him.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان معناه لم يكن هؤلاء الكفار تاركين صفة محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rasūlun min Allāh explains al-bayyina by apposition, an indefinite noun replacing a definite one, as in 85:15–16.
rows.anchor: ثم فسر البينة فقال: رسول من الله. فأبدل النكرة من المعرفة كقوله: ذو العرش المجيد فعال لما يريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yatlū means reads, and ṣuḥuf means books purified of falsehood.
rows.anchor: يتلوا يقرأ صحفا كتبا مطهرة من الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The books contain God's upright, just rulings.
rows.anchor: فيها كتب من الله قيمة مستقيمة عادلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book divided over Muhammad and denied him only after the proof in their scriptures that he was a sent prophet.
rows.anchor: فكذبوه إلا من بعد ما جاءتهم البينة البيان في كتبهم

rows.speaker: قال العلماء
rows.claim: They assign the opening clause to those among the People of the Book and polytheists who believed, and the clause about division to People of the Book who remained unbelievers after the proofs were established.
rows.anchor: قال العلماء: من أول السورة إلى قوله: فيها كتب قيمة حكمها في من آمن

rows.speaker: بعض أئمة أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Another lexical interpretation derives munfakkīn from a phrase for a woman's pelvic separation at childbirth and collapse; the verse then means they were not to be punished until proof came through a messenger and revealed books.
rows.anchor: قوله: منفكين أي هالكين من قوله انفك صلا المرأة عند الولادة

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads wa-l-mushrikūn in the nominative; the source also records variants in the codices of Ibn Masʿūd and Ubayy, including an accusative rasūlan.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش (والمشركون) رفعا، وفي مصحف عبد الله (لم يكن المشركون وأهل الكتاب منفكين)

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy's reading has mā kāna and rasūlan in the accusative as a detached circumstantial expression.
rows.anchor: وفي حرف أبي (ما كان الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب والمشركين منفكين حتى تأتيهم البينة رسولا من الله) بالنصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers were commanded only to worship God sincerely in tawḥīd and obedience, turning from all religions toward Islam.
rows.anchor: وما أمروا يعني هؤلاء الكفار إلا ليعبدوا الله مخلصين يعني إلا أن يعبدوا الله مخلصين له الدين التوحيد والطاعة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He glosses ḥunafāʾ as people performing pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: حجاجا، وقال قتادة:

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He defines ḥanīfiyya through circumcision, prohibiting marriage to close female relatives, and performing the rites.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: الحنيفية هي الختان وتحريم الأمهات والبنات والأخوات والعمات والخالات، وإقامة المناسك.

rows.speaker: سعيد بن حمزة
rows.claim: He says Arabs call someone a ḥanīf only if he performs pilgrimage, is circumcised, and observes the rites.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن حمزة: لا تسمي العرب حنيفا إلا من حج واختتن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer and almsgiving are the upright religion; qayyima is feminine because it refers back to the religious community or law, or its feminine ending intensifies the sense.
rows.anchor: دين القيمة المستقيمة فأضاف الدين إلى القيمة

rows.speaker: أبو سهل محمد بن محمد بن الأشعث الطالقاني
rows.claim: He takes al-qayyima to mean the previously mentioned books, with the religion attributed to those books as what they enjoin; he compares 2:213.
rows.anchor: إن القيمة هاهنا الكتب التي جرى ذكرها، والدين مضاف إليها على معنى: وذلك دين الكتب القيمة

rows.speaker: النضر بن شميل
rows.claim: Reporting al-Khalīl, he explains qayyima as the plural of qayyim or qāʾim: the religion of those who uphold tawḥīd.
rows.anchor: وقال النضر بن شميل: سألت الخليل بن أحمد عن قوله سبحانه: وذلك دين القيمة فقال: القيمة جمع القيم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers are the worst creatures; Nāfiʿ and Ibn Dhakwān read al-bariʾa with hamza on the original form, while other readers omit the hamza and double the consonant.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع البرئة بالهمزة في الحرفين ومثله روى ابن ذكوان عن أهل الشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of the unhamzated reading is that it dropped the hamza and substituted a consonant resembling it.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أنه ترك الهمزة وأدخل الشبه به عوضا منه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation derives bariyya from al-barāʾ, soil, so it means creatures made from soil.
rows.anchor: والآخر أن يكون (فعيلة) من البراء وهو التراب، تقول العرب: بفيك البراء

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: The believers were pleased with God because of His prior care and enabling grace; God is pleased with them by enabling their following the Messenger and accepting his message. Their pleasure is accepting His rulings.
rows.anchor: بما كان سبق لهم من العناية والتوفيق، ورضوا عنه بما من عليهم بمتابعتهم لرسوله،

rows.speaker: محمد بن الفضيل
rows.claim: Relief and rest lie in contentment and certainty; contentment is God's greatest gate and the worshippers' resting place.
rows.anchor: الروح والراحة في الرضا واليقين، والرضا باب الله الأعظم ومستراح العابدين.

rows.speaker: محمد بن حقيق
rows.claim: Contentment has two forms: accepting God as Lord and manager, and accepting what He decrees and determines.
rows.anchor: الرضا ينقسم قسمين: رضا به ورضا عنه، فالرضا به ربا ومدبرا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view defines contentment as relinquishing personal choice.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الرضا رفع الاختيار. ذي النون:

rows.speaker: ذو النون
rows.claim: Contentment is the heart's joy in bitter fate.
rows.anchor: ذي النون: الرضا: سرور القلب لمر القضاء.

rows.speaker: حارث
rows.claim: Contentment is a heart settled beneath the unfolding of divine judgment.
rows.anchor: حارث: الرضا سكون القلب تحت جريان الحكم.

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو الدمشقي
rows.claim: He calls contentment the endpoint of patience.
rows.anchor: أبو عمرو الدمشقي: الرضا نهاية الصبر.

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
rows.claim: Contentment removes aversion from the heart until only happiness and joy remain.
rows.anchor: الرضا خروج الكراهية من القلب حتى لا يكون إلا فرح وسرور.

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Contentment is regarding things so that nothing displeases a person except what displeases their master.
rows.anchor: هو النظر إلى الأشياء يعني الرضا حتى لا يسخطك شيء إلا ما يسخط مولاك.

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Contentment comes from contemplating God's longstanding kindness to the servant, which leads him to abandon resentment.
rows.anchor: هو النظر إلى قديم إحسان الله للعبد فيترك السخط عليه.

rows.speaker: السهمي
rows.claim: He asks: if you are not content with God, how can you ask Him to be content with you?
rows.anchor: إذا كنت لا ترضى عن الله فكيف تسأله الرضا عنك؟.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth will shake violently at the establishment of the Hour; the common reading has kasra on the first zāy.
rows.anchor: إذا زلزلت حركت الأرض حركة شديدة لقيام الساعة زلزالها

rows.speaker: عاصم الجحدري
rows.claim: He reads the first zāy with fatḥa; it is also a verbal noun, like waswās, qalqāl, and jarjār. Another view calls kasra the verbal noun and fatḥa the name.
rows.anchor: يقرأ: إذا زلزلت الأرض زلزالها الزاي مفتوحة وهو مصدر أيضا كالوسواس والقلقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth casts out its dead and treasures and turns them onto its surface.
rows.anchor: وأخرجت الأرض أثقالها موتاها وكنوزها فيقلبها على ظهرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some posit a shifted word order: the earth reports its news, then the human asks what is wrong with it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: في الآية تقديم وتأخير تقديره يومئذ تحدث أخبارها فيقول الإنسان: ما لها.

rows.speaker: قال المفسرون
rows.claim: The earth tells what deeds were done on it: to the believer it recalls worship and obedience, and to the disbeliever sins; its testimony, with the limbs and angels, exposes him despite God's knowledge.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: تخبر الأرض بما عمل عليها من خير أو شر فتقول للمؤمن يوم القيامة:

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet said the earth will report every deed performed on its surface on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «إن الأرض لتخبر يوم القيامة بكل عمل عمل على ظهرها»

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: In a report from Abu Hurayra, the Prophet explains that the earth's news is its testimony against every man and woman for deeds done on its surface, with their date and place.
rows.anchor: ذكر هذه الآية: «يومئذ تحدث أخبارها» فقال: «تدري ما أخبارها؟»

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: His codex reads tubannī akhbārahā, instead of tuḥaddithu akhbārahā.
rows.anchor: وفي حرف ابن مسعود يومئذ تبني أخبارها.

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: He says the Prophet taught that any jinn, human, or stone that hears the call to prayer in open country will testify for the caller.
rows.anchor: قال لي يعني أبا سعيد: يا بني إذا كنت في البوادي فارفع صوتك بالأذان

rows.speaker: أبو أمية
rows.claim: After praying the obligatory prayer in the Sacred Mosque, he moved around to pray elsewhere so those places could testify for him on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: قال قرأت هذه الآية: يومئذ تحدث أخبارها فأردت أن تشهد لي يوم القيامة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inspired or commanded the earth to speak and gave it permission to do so.
rows.anchor: بأن ربك أوحى لها أي أمرها بالكلام

rows.speaker: العجاج
rows.claim: His line uses awḥā to mean that God commanded the earth to settle and stay fixed.
rows.anchor: أوحى لها القرار فاستقرت … وشدها بالراسيات الثبت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والقرظي وابن زيد
rows.claim: They gloss awḥā ilayhā as God revealing or communicating to the earth.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والقرظي وابن زيد: أوحى إليها. ومجاز الآية: يوحي الله إليها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People leave the gathering for judgment in scattered groups: some go rightward to Paradise and some leftward to Hell.
rows.anchor: يومئذ يصدر الناس أشتاتا عن موقف الحساب، أشتاتا: متفرقين فآخذ ذات اليمين إلى الجنة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some propose reordered syntax, putting the earth's report and God's inspiration before the people's departure.
rows.anchor: قيل: في هذه الآية تقديم وتأخير تقديرها يومئذ تحدث أخبارها بأن ربك أوحى لها

rows.speaker: الحسن والأعرج
rows.claim: The common reading has a passive yāʾ in liyuraw, meaning people are shown their deeds; they read it actively with fatḥa, and that reading is also attributed to the Prophet.
rows.anchor:
وقراءة العامة ليروا بضم الياء،
وقرأ الحسن والأعرج بفتح الياء وروي ذلك عن النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever does an atom's weight of good sees its reward; whoever does an atom's weight of evil sees it.
rows.anchor: فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره أي يرى ثوابه ومن يعمل مثقال ذرة شرا يره.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Every believer and disbeliever is shown all their good and evil deeds: believers' sins are forgiven and good rewarded, while disbelievers' good is rejected and evil punished.
rows.anchor: ليس مؤمن ولا كافر عمل خيرا ولا شرا في الدنيا إلا أراه الله إياه،

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: A disbeliever's tiny good is repaid through worldly effects on self, family, wealth, and children, leaving no afterlife good; a believer's tiny evil is punished in worldly life, leaving no afterlife evil.
rows.anchor: فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا من كافر يرى ثوابه في نفسه وأهله وماله وولده

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: When Abu Bakr feared that an atom's weight of evil would be shown, the Prophet said disliked worldly troubles count as tiny evils while God saves the tiny good deeds to repay at the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: «يا أبا بكر ما رأيت في الدنيا مما تكره فبمثاقيل ذر الشر، ويدخر الله لك مثاقيل ذر الخير

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: When Abu Bakr wept at the revelation, the Prophet said that if people never sinned, God would create a people who sin and are forgiven.
rows.anchor: «والله لو أنكم لا تخطئون ولا تذنبون ويغفر الله لكم لخلق الله أمة يخطئون

rows.speaker: خالد بن نشيط وعاصم الجحدري
rows.claim: They read yaraa with the two yāʾs rounded into passive form, matching the passive reading of liyuraw.
rows.anchor: وقرأ خالد بن نشيط وعاصم الجحدري بضم الياءين لقوله: ليروا.

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The verses address two men: one undervalued giving a date, crust, or nut when people were urged to feed others in 76:8; the other dismissed small sins. The passage urges little good and warns that small sins may grow grave.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: نزلت هذه الآية في رجلين وذلك أنه لما نزل ويطعمون الطعام على حبه

rows.speaker: ثعلبة
rows.claim: He explains a dharra as one hundredth of the weight of a seed.
rows.anchor: سئل ثعلبة عن الذرة قال: إن مائة مثل وزن حبة والذرة واحد منها.

rows.speaker: يزيد بن مروان
rows.claim: He transmits the view that a particle has no weight; mīthqāl means weight and is formed from the root for heaviness.
rows.anchor: زعموا أن الذرة ليس لها وزن، ومعنى المثقال الوزن،

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: He calls this the most comprehensive verse in the Qur'an.
rows.anchor:
وقال
ابن مسعود: أحكم آية في القرآن فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet called the passage al-jāmiʿa al-fādha, the comprehensive, singularly encompassing one.
rows.anchor: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يسميها «الجامعة الفاذة»

rows.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
rows.claim: When a recipient closed his hand on two dates Saʿd gave him, Saʿd urged him to accept, saying God might accept even an atom's weight.
rows.anchor: وتصدق سعد بن أبي وقاص بتمرتين وقبض السائل يده فقال سعد:

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وعائشة
rows.claim: Each gave away a single grape and said it held many particles' worth of good.
rows.anchor: وتصدق عمر بن الخطاب وعائشة بحبة من عنب وقالا فيها مثاقيل ذر كثر.

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: An Arab asked twice whether the verse truly meant an atom's weight; he exclaimed in alarm and left repeating it, and the Prophet said faith had entered his heart.
rows.anchor: فقال الأعرابي: يا رسول الله مثقال ذرة؟

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Ṣaʿṣaʿa, al-Farazdaq's uncle, said after hearing the verse that it sufficed him and he needed no more Qur'an.
rows.anchor: فلما سمع فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: A passerby who recited the surah and said he had completed the admonition understood its lesson, al-Hasan says.
rows.anchor:
مر رجل بالحسن وهو يقرأ هذه السورة، فلما بلغ آخرها قال:
«حسبي قد أتممت الموعظة»

rows.speaker: أبو بكر أحمد بن محمد بن إبراهيم الحواربي
rows.claim: His poem restates that people see and are recompensed for good and evil, matching the surah's promise.
rows.anchor:
وزن مثقال ذرة سيراه
ويجازى بفعله الشر شرا

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet defines al-kanūd as an ingrate who eats alone, withholds assistance, and beats his servant.
rows.anchor: [قال: هو الكفور الذي] يأكل وحده، ويمنع رفده، ويضرب عبده»

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Al-kanūd is one who fails to support his people in a calamity.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء: الكنود الذي لا يعطي في النائبة مع قومه.

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Al-kanūd means having little good; barren, unfruitful land is also called kanūd.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: هو قليل الخير، والأرض الكنود التي لا تنبت شيئا

rows.speaker: أبو ذبيان
rows.claim: His poem uses kanūd for an adverse, unproductive stretch of time.
rows.anchor: إن نفسي ولم أطب عنك نفسا

rows.speaker: الفضيل بن عياض
rows.claim: The ungrateful person lets one kindness make him forget many acts of mistreatment.
rows.anchor: وقال الفضيل بن عياض: الكنود الذي أنسته الخصلة الواحدة من الإحسان الخصال الكثيرة من الإساءة.

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
rows.claim: Al-kanūd is someone who attributes blessings to himself and his helpers.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الوراق: الكنود الذي يرى النعمة من نفسه وأعوانه.

rows.speaker: محمد بن علي الترمذي
rows.claim: Al-kanūd sees the blessing but fails to see its giver.
rows.anchor: محمد بن علي الترمذي: هو الذي يرى النعمة ولا يرى المنعم،

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-kanūd spends God's blessings in disobedience to God.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الواسطي: هو الذي ينفق نعم الله سبحانه في معاصي الله،

rows.speaker: بسام بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-kanūd argues with his Lord as though demanding payment in exchange for obedience.
rows.anchor: وقال بسام بن عبد الله: هو الذي يجادل ربه على عقد العوض.

rows.speaker: ذو النون
rows.claim: He links kanūd with the traits in 70:20–21: despair when harmed and withholding when given good.
rows.anchor: ذو النون: تفسير الهلوع والكنود قوله: إذا مسه الشر جزوعا وإذا مسه الخير منوعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other glosses call the person ungrateful for little while failing to thank for much, rancorous, envious, or ignorant of the blessing's worth.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو الذي يكفر باليسير ولا يشكر الكثير، وقيل: الحقود، وقيل: الحسود.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: One description says his head rests on the cushion of blessing while his heart wanders in heedlessness.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم والحسن: رأسه على وسادة النعمة وقلبه في ميدان الغفلة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another description says he sees what comes from himself but not what comes to him; the plural of kanūd is kand.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يرى ما منه ولا يرى ما إليه، وجمع الكنود كند.

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: His verse uses kand of someone who is unresponsive to the customary visitor's affection.
rows.anchor: قال الأعشى: أحدث لها [تحدث] لوصلك أنها … كند لوصل الزائر المعتاد

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators say God witnesses this person's ingratitude and conduct.
rows.anchor: قال أكثر المفسرين: وإن الله على كنود هذا الإنسان وصنيعه لشاهد،

rows.speaker: ابن كيسان
rows.claim: He takes the pronoun to refer to the human being, who bears witness against himself through what he does.
rows.anchor: راجعة إلى الإنسان، يعني أنه شاهد على نفسه بما يصنع،

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: God calls wealth good because people call it good, though it may be impure or unlawful; likewise He calls battle a bad thing because people regard it as bad, as in 3:174.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: سمى الله المال خيرا وعسى أن يكون خبيثا وحراما ولكن الناس يعدونه خيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because of his love of wealth, the person is exceedingly miserly; shadīd and mutashaddid can both describe a miser.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الآية وإنه من أجل حب المال لشديد بخيل، ويقال للبخيل: شديد ومتشدد،

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: His account, transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās and Yemeni authorities, says Dhu Nuwās converted Himyar to Judaism, while Najran's Christians, led by ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Tāmir, refused and chose death; he killed them in trenches and by other means.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق: كان من قصة أصحاب الفيل فيما ذكر بعض أهل العلم عن سعيد ابن جبير وعكرمة عن ابن عباس،

rows.speaker: دوس بن ثعلبان
rows.claim: A man of Saba escaped Dhu Nuwās on horseback, reached Caesar, and sought help; Caesar referred him to the Christian Negus of Abyssinia.
rows.anchor: إلا رجلا من أهل سبأ يقال له دوس بن ثعلبان، فذهب على فرس له

rows.speaker: النجاشي
rows.claim: He sent the Abyssinian Aryat to Yemen with orders to kill a third of its men, ruin a third of its cities, and send him a third of its captives.
rows.anchor: إن دخلت اليمن فاقتل ثلث رجالها، واضرب ثلث بلادها وابعث إلي بثلث سباياها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Aryat conquered Yemen and applied the order, Dhu Nuwās rode into the sea and drowned; a poem laments Yemen and Ghumdan's palace reduced to ashes.
rows.anchor: فاستعرض به البحر فضربه فهلكا جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Aryat stayed in Yemen, Abraha rebelled against him; they agreed to single combat, and Aryat's blow disfigured Abraha's face, earning him the name al-Ashram, before ʿAtūda killed Aryat.
rows.anchor: وكان أرياط جسيما عظيما وسيما، في يده حربته، وكان أبرهة رجلا قصيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Abyssinians rallied behind Abraha; Negus swore to punish him, but Abraha sent his hair and a sack of Yemeni soil in submission, so Negus forgave and confirmed his rule.
rows.anchor:
إليه بجراب من تراب
أرضه ليضعه تحت قدمه

rows.speaker: أبرهة
rows.claim: Abraha built a magnificent church in Sanaa and declared he would redirect the Arabs' pilgrimage there instead of to the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: ثم إن أبرهة بنى كنيسة بصنعاء يقال لها: الفليس، وكتب إلى النجاشي:

rows.speaker: رجل من بني مالك بن كنانة
rows.claim: In response to Abraha's claim, a man from Kinana entered the church at night and defiled it, provoking Abraha.
rows.anchor: فسمع بذلك رجل من بني مالك بن كنانة

rows.speaker: ذو نفر
rows.claim: The Himyari ruler opposed Abraha, lost the battle, and was captured; Abraha spared and bound him after he argued that keeping him alive would be more useful.
rows.anchor: فخرج ملك من ملوك حمير يقال له: ذو نفر بمن أطاعه من قومه، فقابله فهزمه

rows.speaker: نفيل بن حبيب الخثعمي
rows.claim: Nufayl led Khathʿam tribes against Abraha, was defeated, and secured his life by offering submission and local guidance.
rows.anchor: فخرج نفيل بن حبيب الخثعمي في قبيلتي خثعم شهدان وأهش

rows.speaker: مسعود بن مغيث
rows.claim: At Taif, Thaqif told Abraha they would not oppose him and that their shrine to al-Lāt was not the Kaaba he sought; they gave him Abu Righal as a guide, whose grave was later stoned.
rows.anchor: فقال: أيها الملك إنما نحن عبيدك ليس لك عندنا من خلاف،

rows.speaker: الأسود بن مقصود
rows.claim: Abraha sent him ahead to seize the Sanctuary's property; he took two hundred of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib's camels, prompting a curse-poem by ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar al-Makhzūmī.
rows.anchor: فجمع إليه أموال الحرم وأصاب لعبد المطلب مائتي بعير،

rows.speaker: حائلة الحميري
rows.claim: Abraha's envoy told the Meccans that the army came only to destroy the Kaaba, not to fight them unless they resisted.
rows.anchor: أخبره أني لم آت لقتال وإنما لأهدم هذا البيت،

rows.speaker: عبد المطلب
rows.claim: He says Mecca cannot fight Abraha; the Kaaba is God's and Abraham's sanctuary, and its Lord will protect it if He wills.
rows.anchor: فقال عبد المطلب: ما له عندنا وما لنا به نزال، سنخلي بينه وبين ما جاء له،

rows.speaker: ذو نفر
rows.claim: As a prisoner and friend of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, he says he can do little but asks the elephant handler Anīs to help secure him an audience and standing with Abraha.
rows.anchor: فقال: ما غناء رجل أسير لا يأمن أن يقتل بكرة وعشية، ولكني سأبعث لك إلى أنيس سائس الفيل

rows.speaker: أنيس
rows.claim: Anīs commends ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib to Abraha as Quraysh's leader and generous feeder of people and animals, stressing that he comes peacefully.
rows.anchor: هذا سيد قريش وصاحب عير مكة الذي يطعم الناس في السهل والوحوش

rows.speaker: عبد المطلب
rows.claim: Asked his request, he seeks return of his two hundred camels. When Abraha reproaches him for not pleading for the Kaaba, he says he owns the camels while the House has its own Lord; Abraha restores them.
rows.anchor: حاجتي إلى الملك أن يرد علي مائتي بعير أصابها لي،

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: He transmits a report that two leaders offered Abraha a third of Tihama's wealth if he would turn back, but he refused.
rows.anchor:
ذهب إلى أبرهة بعمر بن ناثة بن
عدي بن الويل

rows.speaker: عبد المطلب
rows.claim: He tells Quraysh to take refuge in mountain ravines, then prays at the Kaaba that God defend His sanctuary; his lines warn that the invaders seek to enslave God's dependents.
rows.anchor: أن يتفرقوا في الشعاب، وتحرزوا في رؤوس الجبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elephant was named Maḥmūd and sent by the Negus; some say the army had twelve elephants.
rows.anchor: وكان اسم الفيل محمود، وكان فيل النجاشي بعثه إلى أبرهة،

rows.speaker: نفيل بن حبيب
rows.claim: Nufayl told Maḥmūd to kneel and return because this was God's sacred land; the elephant knelt toward the Sanctuary despite blows and hooks, but moved toward Yemen, Syria, and east when directed elsewhere.
rows.anchor: ابرك محمود وارجع راشدا من حيث جئت، فإنك في بلد الله الحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent sea birds like swallows, each carrying three stones, two in its feet and one in its beak, as small as chickpeas or lentils; every person struck died.
rows.anchor: وأرسل الله طيرا من البحر أمثال الخطاطيف مع كل طاير منها ثلاثة أحجار:

rows.speaker: نفيل بن حبيب
rows.claim: Those who escaped fled asking Nufayl for the road to Yemen; he recited a poem declaring there was nowhere to flee from God and the defeated al-Ashram.
rows.anchor: فقال نفيل بن حبيب حين رأى ما أنزل الله بهم من نقمته: أين المفر والإله الطالب … والأشرم المغلوب غير الغالب؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The army scattered, died along the roads, and suffered severe illness; Abraha's fingers fell away with pus and blood, and he reached Sanaa like a fledgling before his chest split and he died.
rows.anchor: فجعل تتساقط أنامله، كلما سقطت أنملة أتبعتها مدة من قيح ودم،

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
rows.claim: He gives another cause: Quraysh merchants accidentally burned a Christian church by leaving a cooking fire in a windy spot; the enraged Negus sent Abraha to destroy the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: وزعم مقاتل بن سليمان أن السبب الذي جر حديث أصحاب الفيل هو أن قبيلة من قريش خرجوا تجارا

rows.speaker: أبو مسعود الثقفي
rows.claim: The blind Meccan sage advised ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib to consecrate one hundred camels at the Sanctuary, hoping their slaughter would anger the Lord of the House; ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib did so and prayed.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو مسعود لعبد المطلب: اعمد إلى مائة من الإبل فاجعلها حرما لله،

rows.speaker: أبو مسعود الثقفي
rows.claim: He recalls that God protected the Kaaba from the Yemeni king Tubbaʿ, who tried to destroy it; after three days of darkness he honored and clothed it and sacrificed camels.
rows.anchor: إن لهذا البيت لربا يمنعه، فقد نزل تبع ملك اليمن بصخر هذا البيت وأراد هدمه،

rows.speaker: عبد المطلب
rows.claim: ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib describes strange, unfamiliar white sea-birds arriving in flocks, led by a distinctive bird, and circling over the army.
rows.anchor: أرى طيرا بيضا نشأت من شاطئ البحر قال: ارمقها ببصرك أين قرارها؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each bird's stones bore their target's name; the birds dropped them, departed, and the next morning the army lay dead. Stones pierced eggs, skulls, and elephants and buried deeply in the ground.
rows.anchor: مكتوب في كل حجر اسم صاحبه، ثم إنها انصاعت من حيث جاءت،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After discovering gold and jewels in the army's earth, ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib generously shared the treasure with Abu Masʿud and the Meccans; his standing rose, and God defended the Kaaba with forces none could resist.
rows.anchor: وساد عبد المطلب بذلك قريش، وأعطته المقادة فلم يزل عبد المطلب وأبو مسعود

rows.speaker: الواقدي
rows.claim: He says Negus sent Aryat with four thousand men to Yemen; Abraha revolted, killed Aryat, and seized power.
rows.anchor: وقال الواقدي بأسانيده: وجه أبرهة أرياط أبا ضخمة في أربعة آلاف إلى اليمن

rows.speaker: أبرهة
rows.claim: After seeing Arabs travel to Mecca for pilgrimage, he built an elaborate jeweled church and directed Arabs to worship and pilgrimage there; many did so for years.
rows.anchor: فرأى الناس يتجهزون للحج فقال: أين يذهب الناس؟ قال: يحجون بيت الله بمكة.

rows.speaker: نفيل الخثعمي
rows.claim: Opposed to Abraha's church, Nufayl defiled it with excrement and carcasses; Abraha blamed Arab devotion to their own House and requested the Negus's elephant Maḥmūd.
rows.anchor: فجاء بعذرة فلطخ بها جبهته، وجمع جيفا وألقاها فيه،

rows.speaker: عبد المطلب
rows.claim: In the continuing account, Abraha's force raided the Sanctuary's herds and took his camels; after they were restored he marked them as offerings and left them in the Haram, praying for God to protect His own sanctuary.
rows.anchor: فأصابوا إبلا لعبد المطلب، وكان نفيل صديقا لعبد المطلب فكلمه في إبله،

rows.speaker: عبد المطلب
rows.claim: He marks the returned camels as offerings and prays that God protect His sanctuary, as a person protects his own property.
rows.anchor: اللهم إن المرء يمنع رحله وحلاله فامنع حلالك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Birds pelted the army with stones that crushed them; a torrent swept them to the sea. This was the first observed outbreak of smallpox and measles, while Abraha's body deteriorated.
rows.anchor: وقذفت الحجارة عليهم، لا تصيب شيئا إلا هشمته إلا فقط ذلك الموضع،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Negus's elephant Maḥmūd knelt and survived without attacking the Sanctuary; another elephant advanced and was pelted, and some say there were twelve elephants.
rows.anchor: وأما محمود فيل النجاشي فربض ولم يشجع على الحرم فنجا،

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: After the Abyssinians were repelled, Arabs honored Quraysh as God's protected people; a poem says God halted the elephant and glosses mukarkas as overturned and thrown down.
rows.anchor: ولما رد الله الحبشة عن مكة عظمت العرب قريشا وقالوا: أهل الله، قاتل عنهم

rows.speaker: أبو الصلت بن أمية بن مسعود
rows.claim: His poem presents the halted elephant and fleeing army as enduring signs of God, with the soldiers' limbs broken.
rows.anchor: ما يماري فيهن إلا الكفور

rows.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
rows.claim: They say Abu Yaksum was Abraha's companion and minister; all perished except him, but a bird killed him as he reported the disaster to the Negus.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي ومقاتل: كان صاحب الجيش أبرهة، وكان أبو يكسوم من وزرائه وندمائه،

rows.speaker: الآخرون
rows.claim: Other authorities identify Abu Yaksum as Abraha ibn al-Sabbah.
rows.anchor: وقال الآخرون: أبو يكسوم هو أبرهة بن الصباح.

rows.speaker: الواقدي
rows.claim: He says Abraha was the grandfather of the Negus who lived in the Prophet's time.
rows.anchor: وقال الواقدي: كان أبرهة جد النجاشي الذي كان في زمن رسول الله

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: He dates the Elephant expedition forty years before the Prophet's birth.
rows.anchor: فقال مقاتل: كان أمر الفيل قبل مولد رسول الله

rows.speaker: الكلبي وعبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: They date the event twenty-three years before the Prophet's birth.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي وعبيد بن عمير: كان قبل مولد النبي

rows.speaker: أكثر العلماء
rows.claim: Most scholars place the expedition in the year the Prophet was born, supported by Qubāth ibn Ashyam's statement that Muhammad was born that year and Qubāth was older.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه كان في العام الذي ولد فيه رسول الله

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: She says she saw the elephant's blind, crippled handler and driver in Mecca begging.
rows.anchor: وقالت عائشة: رأيت قائد الفيل وسائسه بمكة عميين مقعدين يستطعمان.

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: He says the invading force had one elephant; al-Dahhak says eight, perhaps to match the verse endings, or they were named after the lead elephant Maḥmūd.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: كان معهم فيل واحد، وقال الضحاك: كانت ثمانية،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The army's plot was thwarted in its attempt to destroy the Kaaba; another gloss takes it as nullity or loss.
rows.anchor: ألم يجعل كيدهم في تضليل عما أرادوا من تخريب الكعبة:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abābīl means many dispersed birds, one group following another, coming from the sea.
rows.anchor: وأرسل عليهم من البحر طيرا أبابيل كثيرة متفرقة، يتبع بعضها بعضا.

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن إيزي
rows.claim: He glosses abābīl as flocks like advancing camels.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الرحمن بن ايزي: أقاطيع كالإبل المقبلة.

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: His poetry uses abābīl of flocks of birds calling as they pass.
rows.anchor: عليه أبابيل من الطير تنعب

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: His poetry likens a rushing crowd to flocks of birds beneath a dark cloud.
rows.anchor: أبابيل طير تحت دجن مسخن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another poet uses al-abābīl for swarms of cavalry sweeping over the land.
rows.anchor: أن سالت الأرض بالجرد الأبابيل

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says abābīl has no singular, like shamāṭīṭ, abābīd, and shaʿārīr.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: لا واحد لها مثل الشماطيط والعباديد والشعارير

rows.speaker: أبو الرواسي
rows.claim: He reports hearing ibāla as a singular and cites the expression a burden upon a burden.
rows.anchor: قال: وزعم أبو الرواسي وكان ثقة مأمونا أنه سمع واحدها إبالة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He identifies ʿaṣf as the crop's tips before it forms ears.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: لا واحد لها مثل الشماطيط والعباديد والشعارير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A proposed singular is ibāla, by analogy with dīnār/danānīr; the word can also mean fodder or an extra load on a donkey or camel.
rows.anchor: ولو قال قائل: واحدها إبالة كان صوابا مثل دينار ودنانير،

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: The grammarians he heard used ibūl as the singular, by analogy with ʿajūl and ʿajāʾīl.
rows.anchor:
وقال الكسائي: كنت أسمع النحويين يقولون:
واحدها إبول

rows.speaker: محمد بن جرير
rows.claim: He transmits another grammarian's proposed singular, abīl, for groups of horses coming from different directions.
rows.anchor: وحكى محمد بن جرير عن بعض النحويين أن واحدها أبيل،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He describes the birds as having beaks like birds' bills and feet like dogs' paws.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لها خراطيم كخراطيم الطير وأكف كأكف الكلاب.

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: He says the birds had heads like beasts of prey, unlike any seen before or afterward.
rows.anchor: عكرمة: لها رؤوس كرءوس السباع لم تر قبل ذلك ولا بعده.

rows.speaker: ربيع
rows.claim: He says the birds had teeth like beasts of prey.
rows.anchor: ربيع: لها أنياب كأنياب السباع،

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: She says they most resembled swallows.
rows.anchor: وقالت عائشة: أشبه شيء بالخطاطيف.

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: He describes green birds with yellow beaks.
rows.anchor: سعيد بن جبير: طير خضر لها مناقير صفر،

rows.speaker: أبو الجوزاء
rows.claim: He says God created the birds in the air at that moment.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الجوزاء: أنشأها الله سبحانه في الهواء في ذلك الوقت.

rows.speaker: طلحة وأشهب العقيلي
rows.claim: They read yarīmuhum with yāʾ rather than the common tāʾ; Abū Ḥanīfa prefers that reading, taking God as subject, as in 8:17.
rows.anchor: وقرأ طلحة وأشهب العقيلي يرميهم بالياء، وهو اختيار أبي حنيفة، يعنون الله سبحانه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The yāʾ reading can also refer to the birds, since the word has no feminine marker.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون راجعا إلى الطير لخلوها من علامات التأنيث.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent a wind that strengthened the stones; each one pierced its victim and exited the other side, including through the head and rear.
rows.anchor: وبعث الله سبحانه ريحا فضربت الحجارة فزادتها شدة، فما وقع منها حجر على رجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The army was like chewed crop: beasts eat it, digest it, and scatter the dried parts, just as the soldiers' bodies were torn apart.
rows.anchor: فجعلهم كعصف مأكول كزرع أكلته الدواب فراثته فيبس وتفرقت أجزاؤه،

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He glosses ʿaṣf as wheat leaves.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: العصف: ورق الحنطة.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He glosses ʿaṣf as straw.
rows.anchor: قتادة: هو التبن، قال الحسن

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He says barley stalks were called ʿaṣf in Medina when he was a boy.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: كنا ونحن غلمان بالمدينة نأكل الشعير إذا قصب وكان يسمى العصف.

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: He says it is sprouted barley whose leaves are eaten.
rows.anchor: سعيد بن جبير: هو الشعير النابت الذي يؤكل ورقه.

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: He likens the army to a mountain eaten hollow.
rows.anchor: عكرمة: كالجبل إذا أكل فصار أجوف.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He identifies ʿaṣf as the husk enveloping a wheat grain.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: هو القشر الخارج الذي يكون على حب الحنطة

rows.speaker: المؤرخ
rows.claim: He calls it broken crop whose tips have fallen off.
rows.anchor: المؤرخ: هو ما يقصف من الزرع فسقطت أطرافه،

rows.speaker: ابن السكيت
rows.claim: He groups ʿaṣf with ʿaṣīfa and jill as related terms.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن السكيت: هو العصف والعصيفة والجل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss is crop whose grain has been eaten while its straw remains; al-Daḥḥāk glosses it as food that has been eaten.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كزرع قد أكل حبه وبقي تبنه، وقال الضحاك: كطعام مطعوم.

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عامر
rows.claim: He reads laʾalāf, with hamza and without yāʾ; Abū Jaʿfar is reported to read īlāf without hamza for ease, while the common form has a full hamza and yāʾ.
rows.anchor: فقرأ عبد الله بن عامر (لألاف) مهموزا مختلسا بلا ياء، وقرأ أبو جعفر (ايلاف) بغير همز

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن كثير
rows.claim: A report from al-ʿUmari and al-Balkhi gives their reading as ilfahum, with a still lām and no yāʾ; a report from Asmāʾ says the Prophet read it that way.
rows.anchor: فروى العمري عن أبي جعفر والبلخي عن ابن كثير (إلفهم) ساكنة اللام يغير ياء

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Asmāʾ reports hearing the Prophet recite ilfahum for the winter and summer journey.
rows.anchor: عن أسماء قالت: سمعت النبي

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وأهل الشام
rows.claim: They are reported to read ilāfahum with a lightly articulated hamza and no yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وروى الفضل بن شاذان بإسناده عن أبي جعفر، والوليد عن أهل الشام (إلافهم)

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: He is reported to read with two hamzas, the first kasra and the second sukūn; the remaining readers use īlāfahum.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بكر عن عاصم (إألافهم) بهمزتين الأولى مكسورة والثانية ساكنة

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: He reads ilīlāf Quraysh ilfahum, a variant connecting the forms.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة أنه كان يقرأ (إليالف قريش الفهم)

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Some counted Quraysh and the Elephant as one surah; Ubayy's codex has no separator between them, and Sufyan reports an imam who recited both together.
rows.anchor: وعد بعضهم السورتين واحدة منهم أبي بن كعب ولا فصل بينهما في مصحفه.

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: ʿAmr ibn Maymūn says he heard ʿUmar recite al-Tīn in one Maghrib rakʿa and al-Fīl together with Quraysh in the next.
rows.anchor: وقال عمرو بن ميمون الأودي صليت المغرب خلف عمر بن الخطاب

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He links the opening lām to the Elephant surah: the defeat of the army was a favor enabling Quraysh's winter and summer trade; the lām means toward or in addition to.
rows.anchor: فقال الفراء: هي متصلة بالسورة الأولى وذلك أنه [تعالى] ذكر أهل مكة عظيم نعمته عليهم

rows.speaker: الرازي والأخفش
rows.claim: They take the lām as one of astonishment: marvel that Quraysh travel and neglect worship of the House's Lord, whom they are then ordered to worship.
rows.anchor: وقال الرازي والأخفش: هي لام التعجب يقول: عجبوا لإيلاف قريش رحلة الشتاء والصيف،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poem illustrates the lām of astonishment through the phrase about being amazed at Qurra as a poet.
rows.anchor: لإظهار الفعل فيه كقول الشاعر:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view makes the lām purposive: the destruction of the Elephant army preserved Quraysh's security, cohesion, and livelihood.
rows.anchor: وقيل هي لام (كي) مجازها فجعلهم كعصف مأكول ليؤلف قريشا،

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He connects the lām to the following command, meaning they should worship the Lord of the House because of the two trade journeys.
rows.anchor:
وقال الزجاج: هي مردودة إلى ما بعدها، تقديره: ليعبدوا رب هذا البيت
لإيلاف رحلة الشتاء والصيف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh are the descendants of al-Naḍr ibn Kināna; anyone descended from him is Qurashī, while one not descended from him is not.
rows.anchor: وقريش هم ولد النضر بن كنانة، فمن ولده النضر فهو قرشي،

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet says his people descend from al-Naḍr ibn Kināna and do not disavow their mother or father.
rows.anchor: «نحن بنو النضر بن كنانة لا نقفو أمنا، ولا ننتفي من أبينا»

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Wāthila reports that God chose Kināna from Ishmael's descendants, Quraysh from Kināna, Hāshim from Quraysh, and the Prophet from Hāshim.
rows.anchor: «إن الله عز وجل اصطفى بني كنانة من بني كنانة من بني إسماعيل، واصطفى من بني كنانة قريشا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh is linked to taqarrush, acquiring, turning about, gathering, and seeking; the tribe was eager for wealth and generosity.
rows.anchor: وسموا قريشا من التقرش، وهو التكسب والتقلب والجمع والطلب،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He tells Muʿāwiya that Quraysh is named after a predatory sea creature that eats without being eaten and dominates other creatures, as the cited poem says Quraysh consume lands.
rows.anchor:
لدابة في البحر يقال لها:
القرش، تأكل ولا تؤكل، وتعلو ولا تعلا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The last lines of the cited poem say Quraysh will have a prophet in the end times and describe his military reach.
rows.anchor: ولهم آخر الزمان نبي … يكثر القتل فيهم والخموشا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second īlāf is apposition to the first, while dropping yāʾ is supported by Abū Ṭālib's line urging Abū Lahab not to abandon the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقوله: إيلافهم بدل من الإيلاف الأول

rows.speaker: أبو طالب
rows.claim: His poem uses ilāf without yāʾ as it urges Abū Lahab to protect the Prophet and calls the family the best in the world.
rows.anchor: إلا فهم في الناس خير إلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He gives four parses for riḥlata: verbal noun, object of īlāf, adverb with an understood ʿalā, or nominative as the two journeys; he prefers the verbal-noun reading.
rows.anchor: والأول أعجب وأحب إلي لأنها مكتوبة في المصاحف بغير ياء.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ikrima and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr report from him that Quraysh spent winter in Mecca and summer in Taif; God commanded them to winter in the Sanctuary and worship its Lord.
rows.anchor: فروى عكرمة وسعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال: كانوا يشتون بمكة ويصيفون بالطائف،

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: He says Quraysh made two annual trade trips: in winter to warm Yemen and in summer to cool Syria.
rows.anchor: وكانوا يرتحلون في الشتاء إلى الحارة، وفي الصيف إلى الباردة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Haram was barren, without crops, pasture, water, or trees; Quraysh lived by trade and journeying and were protected from attack.
rows.anchor: وكان الحرم واديا جدبا لا زرع فيه ولا ضرع، ولا ماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trade journeys were essential to life in barren Mecca, but nearby harvests in Yemen and Syria supplied food via Jeddah and the local routes, easing the burden of the journeys; God then commanded worship of the House's Lord.
rows.anchor: فامتاروا من قريب وكفاهم الله مؤونة الرحلتين وأمرهم بعبادة رب البيت

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: In a report from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, the Prophet corrects a poem's praise of Banū ʿAbd al-Dār to Banū ʿAbd Manāf, describing their generosity to guests and winter and summer trade journeys.
rows.anchor: لأبي بكر: «أهكذا قال الشاعر يا أبا بكر؟» قال: لا،

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: He says Hāshim ibn ʿAbd Manāf was the first to bring wheat from Syria and drive camels there.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: وكان أول من حمل السمراء من الشام ورحل إليها الإبل هاشم بن عبد مناف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in fal-yaʿbudū is an imperative.
rows.anchor:
يعبدوا
لام الأمر رب هذا البيت

rows.speaker: ابن ملك بن دينار
rows.claim: He says that when a community falls from God's regard, He strikes them with hunger.
rows.anchor: ما سقطت أمة من عين الله سبحانه إلا ضرب أكبادها بالجوع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh were safe because they were residents and guardians of God's Sanctuary; even an Arab caught in another tribe could invoke the Haram and be released, while other tribes were raided.
rows.anchor: وآمنهم من خوف وذلك أنهم كانوا يقولون: نحن قطان حرم الله سبحانه، فلا يعرض لهم أحد

rows.speaker: الضحاك والربيع وشريك وسفيان
rows.claim: They interpret security as protection from leprosy in Mecca.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك والربيع وشريك وسفيان: وآمنهم من الجذام، فلا يصيبهم ببلدهم الجذام.

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says Medina's dust cures leprosy.
rows.anchor: «غبار المدينة يبرئ من الجذام»

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali interprets their security as assurance that the caliphate would remain among Quraysh.
rows.anchor: وقال علي كرم الله وجهه: وآمنهم من [خوف] أن تكون الخلافة إلا فيهم
